request.deadline: Contract year covering 2026-2027; ongoing maintenance and user support for 52 weeks; architecture assessment by Q3 2027
deliverables: Protocol maintenance including cardano-node/cardano-wallet upgrades, hard fork readiness, platform support, release engineering, and security/dependency maintenance
Compatible Daedalus release at least 2 weeks before each mainnet hard fork
Leios, Peras, and Nested Transactions readiness
Keystone and Flex hardware wallet support
User support including Japanese-language support and full Japanese translation maintenance
Independent financial audit and return of unspent labor, hardware, and audit budgets
request.recipient: Se7en Labs, Inc., administered through Intersect with milestone-based monthly disbursements
request.what: Daedalus Wallet Maintenance and Improvements 2026-2027 delivered by Se7en Labs, Inc.

claims.claim: Daedalus is Cardano's only full-node desktop wallet and derives wallet and governance data directly from the chain without third-party APIs or trusted backends.
Daedalus has approximately 4,000 monthly active users according to opt-in telemetry, with the proposer asserting true usage is meaningfully higher.
Se7en Labs has operated under an IOG contract for Daedalus maintenance since January 2026 and shipped Daedalus 8.0 and 11.0 during that period.
The proposed work includes protocol maintenance, hard fork readiness, hardware wallet support, CIP-30, Japanese localisation, user support, and an architecture assessment.
All release-timing and version-currency success metrics are independently verifiable from public GitHub repositories and the Cardano mainnet chain.
The requested withdrawal is 1,785,333 ADA, allocated to 1,666,667 ADA for team labor, 33,333 ADA for test hardware, 33,333 ADA for financial audit, and 52,000 ADA for Intersect administration.
The proposer says the withdrawal does not breach the applicable 350M Net Change Limit covering Epoch 613 to Epoch 713 at the moment of submission.
Intersect will administer the funds, independently verify milestones, hold funds in a dedicated auditable account, and disburse monthly against verified work.
The proposal states that Daedalus is Apache 2.0 open-source software and that all funded outputs will remain public, forkable assets in perpetuity.
The proposal asserts that CIP-30 would enable full-node Daedalus users to interact with compatible dApps without switching to a browser wallet or introducing an external API dependency.

summary: The proposal requests 1,785,333 ADA for a 2026-2027 time-and-materials engagement to maintain and improve Daedalus, with Intersect administration, milestone verification, public deliverables, and several externally checkable success metrics.
